title: The Heavyweight Difference: Why We Stopped Using Thin 150 GSM Blanks
excerpt: Most online t-shirts feel paper-thin after two washes. Here is why 240+ GSM combed ringspun cotton creates the structured drape you actually want.
author: The Tee Drop Editorial Team
content:
When you hold a truly well-made t-shirt, you feel it immediately. The weight, the balance across the shoulders, and the way the fabric falls straight without clinging or twisting sideways.

For years, mass-market apparel brands have cut corners by printing on lightweight 140–160 GSM blends. They feel okay in the showroom, but after a single machine wash, the collar ripples like bacon and the seams twist diagonally across your torso.

What Does 240 GSM Actually Mean?

GSM stands for grams per square meter. A 240 GSM combed ringspun cotton fabric provides enough structural density to hold an intentional drop-shoulder silhouette. It shields against chilly breezes, sits cleanly over athletic physiques, and provides an ultra-flat printing canvas that allows Direct-to-Garment inks to bond deep into each strand without cracking.

How We Source Our Blanks

Every piece in our drops is spun from long-staple combed cotton, pre-shrunk before cutting, and stitched with reinforced twin-needle hems. It is apparel made to be worn hundreds of times, not thrown away next season.

title: How to Style Oversized Graphic Tees (Without Drowning in Fabric)
excerpt: A relaxed fit looks effortless when balanced correctly. Three simple styling rules for street, gym, and casual weekend wear.
author: Sam R., Creative Lead
content:
The oversized graphic tee is one of the most versatile staples in modern menswear and unisex fashion. But there is a fine line between looking intentionally relaxed and looking like you borrowed someone else’s shirt by accident.

Rule 1: Proportional Balance

If your top has an extra-roomy boxy drape, balance it with tapered or straight-leg bottoms. Cargo pants with subtle ankle tapering, raw selvedge denim, or tailored athletic shorts keep your silhouette balanced.

Rule 2: Let the Graphic Anchor the Outfit

Our designs are intentionally bold. Keep the rest of your outfit muted: chalk white sneakers, charcoal or washed black trousers, and minimalist accessories allow the artwork to speak for itself without visual clutter.

Rule 3: Mind the Shoulder Seam

A true drop-shoulder cut is designed to fall 2 to 3 inches below your natural shoulder point while maintaining a collar that stays flat against your neck. You get the relaxed drape without looking sloppy.

title: Wash Cold, Hang Dry: The Complete Care Guide to Keep Your Prints Intact
excerpt: How to preserve water-based DTG inks and avoid collar warping for 60+ washes.
author: Print Shop Team
content:
Water-based Direct-to-Garment (DTG) printing offers vivid, breathable color that doesn’t feel like a plastic sticker stuck to your chest. To ensure your print looks just as vibrant after 50 washes as it did on day one, follow these simple care steps:

  • Flip it inside out: Before tossing your tee into the hamper, turn it inside out. This prevents other zippers or buttons from abrading the graphic surface during agitation.
  • Cold water only (30°C / 85°F): High heat breaks down cotton fibers and causes color bleed. Cold water cleans just as effectively with modern detergents.
  • Air dry when possible: Tumble dryers are the number one cause of fabric shrinkage. Hang your shirt on a wooden or padded hanger to air dry naturally.
  • Never iron directly on print: If you need to iron out wrinkles, iron from the inside out or place a thin cotton tea towel over the artwork.
